title: Rice Dumplings
synopsis: Have you eaten rice dumplings during the Dragon Boat Festival?

fullText.simplified:
粽子的千年

    端午节吃粽子，是中国的传统习俗。
    粽子，是中国的传统美食。说起粽子，它的历史真是讲也讲不完，最著名的莫过于“纪念屈原”这个民间传说。屈原是战国时期楚国的诗人，他因为自己的祖国被攻占而伤心欲绝，所以在五月初五端午节那天跳河自杀了。百姓们很喜欢屈原，为了不让鱼虾们把他的身体吃了，就把粽子投入江中。由此，端午节吃粽子渐渐地成为了中国重要的节日习俗。
    这个传说大家都知道。但其实，粽子的历史还不止这些。
    早在春秋之前，粽子就出现了。那时候的粽子，主要是用来祭祀祖先和神灵的。人们把粽子包成牛角状，因为那时候的人们喜欢在祭祀时用带角的动物作祭品，认为动物的角，是沟通人与神之间的灵物。所以，粽子也要是牛角状的。
    到了隋唐，粽子出现了不同的形状，有菱形、锥形等。端午节人们喜欢吃“九子粽”，就是用彩线把九个粽子系在一起，寓意着“多子多孙”。
    宋朝时期，粽子的内馅开始丰富起来，里面有银杏、赤豆等。
    后来到了明清时期，粽子被赋予了吉祥的含义，人们喜欢在科举考试前吃粽子，讨个好兆头。比如，参加科举考试的人会在考试前吃红枣馅的粽子，那样的粽子被称为“枣粽”，是“早中”的谐音，有“早早中举”的寓意；还有的人喜欢吃做成笔形状的粽子，“笔粽”——“必中”，有“必定高中”的寓意。
    粽子发展至今，形状、味道都发生了很大的变化。现在的粽子，长形、方形、菱形、锥形……各种形状的都有。北方人吃甜粽、南方人吃咸粽，甚至还有苦粽、辣粽、酸粽，各种味道的都有。真是小小的粽子，承载着中国几千年的历史与变迁啊！
fullText.traditional:
粽子的千年

    端午節吃粽子，是中國的傳統習俗。
    粽子，是中國的傳統美食。說起粽子，它的歷史真是講也講不完，最著名的莫過於“紀念屈原”這個民間傳說。屈原是戰國時期楚國的詩人，他因為自己的祖國被攻占而傷心欲絕，所以在五月初五端午節那天跳河自殺了。百姓們很喜歡屈原，為了不讓魚蝦們把他的身體吃了，就把粽子投入江中。由此，端午節吃粽子漸漸地成為了中國重要的節日習俗。
    這個傳說大家都知道。但其實，粽子的歷史還不止這些。
    早在春秋之前，粽子就出現了。那時候的粽子，主要是用來祭祀祖先和神靈的。人們把粽子包成牛角狀，因為那時候的人們喜歡在祭祀時用帶角的動物作祭品，認為動物的角，是溝通人與神之間的靈物。所以，粽子也要是牛角狀的。
    到了隋唐，粽子出現了不同的形狀，有菱形、錐形等。端午節人們喜歡吃“九子粽”，就是用彩線把九個粽子繫在一起，寓意著“多子多孫”。
    宋朝時期，粽子的內餡開始豐富起來，裡面有銀杏、赤豆等。
    後來到了明清時期，粽子被賦予了吉祥的含義，人們喜歡在科舉考試前吃粽子，討個好兆頭。比如，參加科舉考試的人會在考試前吃紅棗餡的粽子，那樣的粽子被稱為“棗粽”，是“早中”的諧音，有“早早中舉”的寓意；還有的人喜歡吃做成筆形狀的粽子，“筆粽”——“必中”，有“必定高中”的寓意。
    粽子發展至今，形狀、味道都發生了很大的變化。現在的粽子，長形、方形、菱形、錐形……各種形狀的都有。北方人吃甜粽、南方人吃鹹粽，甚至還有苦粽、辣粽、酸粽，各種味道的都有。真是小小的粽子，承載著中國幾千年的歷史與變遷啊！

sentences.traditional: 百姓們很喜歡屈原，為了不讓魚蝦們把他的身體吃了，

sentences.traditional: 就把粽子投入江中。

sentences.english: Ordinary people liked Qu Yuan very much, so in order to not let the fish and shrimp eat his body, ..

sentences.traditional: 由此，端午節吃粽子漸漸地成為了中國重要的節日習俗。

sentences.english: Everyone knows this legend. But in fact, the story of rice dumplings doesn’t end with this.

sentences.pinyin: zǎo zài chūn qiū zhī qián zòng zi jiù chū xiàn le

sentences.traditional: 那時候的粽子，主要是用來祭祀祖先和神靈的。

sentences.traditional: 因為那時候的人們喜歡在祭祀時用帶角的動物作祭品，

sentences.english: People wrapped rice dumplings into the shape of cow horns, ..

sentences.simplified: 认为动物的角，是沟通人与神之间的灵物。
sentences.traditional: 認為動物的角，是溝通人與神之間的靈物。
sentences.pinyin: rèn wéi dòng wù de jiǎo shì gōu tōng rén yǔ shén zhī jiān de líng wù
sentences.english: .. because the people at that time liked to use animals that had horns as offerings when they sacrificed.

sentences.simplified: 所以，粽子也要是牛角状的。
sentences.traditional: 所以，粽子也要是牛角狀的。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ zòng zi yě yào shì niú jiǎo zhuàng de
sentences.english: They believed that animal horns were a spiritual thing to communicate between people and spirits.
Therefore, rice dumplings also had to be cow horn-shaped.

sentences.simplified: 到了隋唐，粽子出现了不同的形状，有菱形、锥形等。
sentences.traditional: 到了隋唐，粽子出現了不同的形狀，有菱形、錐形等。
sentences.pinyin: dào le suí táng zòng zi chū xiàn le bù tóng de xíng zhuàng yǒu líng xíng zhuī xíng děng

sentences.simplified: 端午节人们喜欢吃“九子粽”，

sentences.pinyin: duān wǔ jié rén men xǐ huan chī jiǔ zi zòng
sentences.english: By the Sui and Tang dynasties, rice dumplings appeared in different shapes. They were rhombus, conical and so on.

sentences.simplified: 就是用彩线把九个粽子系在一起，寓意着“多子多孙”。
sentences.traditional: 就是用彩線把九個粽子繫在一起，寓意著“多子多孫”。
sentences.pinyin: jiù shì yòng cǎi xiàn bǎ jiǔ ge zòng zi jì zài yì qǐ yù yì zhe duō zǐ duō sūn
sentences.english: At the Dragon Boat Festival people like to eat “Nine Rice Dumplings”,
This is nine rice dumplings tied together with brightly colored string, implying “many descendants”.

sentences.simplified: 宋朝时期，粽子的内馅开始丰富起来，
sentences.traditional: 宋朝時期，粽子的內餡開始豐富起來，

sentences.traditional: 裡面有銀杏、赤豆等。
sentences.pinyin: lǐ miàn yǒu yín xìng chì dòu děng
sentences.english: In the Song dynasty period, the inside filling of rice dumplings started getting plentiful.
They had ginkgo, red bean and so on inside.

sentences.simplified: 后来到了明清时期，粽子被赋予了吉祥的含义，
sentences.traditional: 後來到了明清時期，粽子被賦予了吉祥的含義，
sentences.pinyin: hòu lái dào le míng qīng shí qī zòng zi bèi fù yǔ le jí xiáng de hán yì

sentences.simplified: 人们喜欢在科举考试前吃粽子，讨个好兆头。
sentences.traditional: 人們喜歡在科舉考試前吃粽子，討個好兆頭。
sentences.pinyin: rén men xǐ huan zài kē jǔ kǎo shì qián chī zòng zi tǎo ge hǎo zhào tou
sentences.english: In the later Ming and Qing dynasty periods, rice dumplings were assigned with auspicious connotations.

sentences.simplified: 比如，参加科举考试的人
sentences.traditional: 比如，參加科舉考試的人
sentences.pinyin: bǐ rú cān jiā kē jǔ kǎo shì de rén
sentences.english: People liked to eat rice dumplings before exams at the imperial examinations, asking for a good omen.

sentences.simplified: 会在考试前吃红枣馅的粽子，
sentences.traditional: 會在考試前吃紅棗餡的粽子，
sentences.pinyin: huì zài kǎo shì qián chī hóng zǎo xiàn de zòng zi
sentences.english: For example, people that were participating in the exams at the imperial examinations, ..

sentences.simplified: 那样的粽子被称为“枣粽”，是“早中”的谐音，
sentences.traditional: 那樣的粽子被稱為“棗粽”，是“早中”的諧音，
sentences.pinyin: nà yàng de zòng zi bèi chēng wéi zǎo zòng shì zǎo zhòng de xié yīn
sentences.english: .. would eat a rice dumpling with a red date filling before the exams.

sentences.simplified: 有“早早中举”的寓意；
sentences.traditional: 有“早早中舉”的寓意；
sentences.pinyin: yǒu zǎo zǎo zhòng jǔ de yù yì
sentences.english: That kind of rice dumplings is called “zao zong”, which is a homophone to “hit the mark soon”.

sentences.simplified: 还有的人喜欢吃做成笔形状的粽子，
sentences.traditional: 還有的人喜歡吃做成筆形狀的粽子，
sentences.pinyin: hái yǒu de rén xǐ huan chī zuò chéng bǐ xíng zhuàng de zòng zi
sentences.english: It implies “passing the provincial-level imperial examination soon”;

sentences.simplified: “笔粽”——“必中”，有“必定高中”的寓意。
sentences.traditional: “筆粽”——“必中”，有“必定高中”的寓意。
sentences.pinyin: bǐ zòng bì zhòng yǒu bì dìng gāo zhòng de yù yì
sentences.english: There were also people that liked to eat rice dumplings that were made into a pen shape.
“Bi zong” – “certainly hit the mark”, implies “to be bound to pass brilliantly”.

sentences.simplified: 粽子发展至今，形状、味道都发生了很大的变化。
sentences.traditional: 粽子發展至今，形狀、味道都發生了很大的變化。

sentences.simplified: 现在的粽子，长形、方形、菱形、锥形……各种形状的都有。
sentences.traditional: 現在的粽子，長形、方形、菱形、錐形……各種形狀的都有。

sentences.english: Rice dumplings have developed to this day, and very big changes have happened with both shape and flavor.

sentences.traditional: 北方人吃甜粽、南方人吃鹹粽，

sentences.english: Present rice dumplings are long-shaped, square-shaped, rhombus, conical... there are all kinds of shapes.

sentences.simplified: 甚至还有苦粽、辣粽、酸粽，各种味道的都有。
sentences.traditional: 甚至還有苦粽、辣粽、酸粽，各種味道的都有。
sentences.pinyin: shèn zhì hái yǒu kǔ zòng là zòng suān zòng gè zhǒng wèi dào de dōu yǒu
sentences.english: Northern people eat sweet rice dumplings, southern people eat salty rice dumplings.

sentences.simplified: 真是小小的粽子，承载着中国几千年的历史与变迁啊！
sentences.traditional: 真是小小的粽子，承載著中國幾千年的歷史與變遷啊！
sentences.pinyin: zhēn shì xiǎo xiǎo de zòng zi chéng zài zhe zhōng guó jǐ qiān nián de lì shǐ yǔ biàn qiān a
sentences.english: There are even bitter rice dumplings, spicy rice dumplings, sour rice dumplings, all kinds of flavors as well.
They really are very small rice dumplings that bear the weight of several thousand years of Chinese history and change!

raw.synopsis: Have you eaten rice dumplings during the Dragon Boat Festival?
sentence_translations: A Thousand Years of Rice Dumplings
To eat rice dumplings at the Dragon Boat Festival, is a Chinese tradition.
Rice dumplings are a traditional Chinese delicacy.
When speaking of rice dumplings, you truly never run out of stories to tell about them.
The most well-known above all others is this popular legend “To Commemorate Qu Yuan”.
Qu Yuan was a Chu poet of the Warring States period.
He was inconsolably heartbroken because his own motherland had been seized, ..
.. so during the Dragon Boat Festival on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month, he jumped in a river to commit suicide.
Ordinary people liked Qu Yuan very much, so in order to not let the fish and shrimp eat his body, ..
.. they took rice dumplings and threw them into the river.
From this, eating rice dumplings at the Dragon Boat Festival gradually became an important Chinese holiday tradition.
Everyone knows this legend. But in fact, the story of rice dumplings doesn’t end with this.
Rice dumplings emerged long ago before the Spring and Autumn period.
The rice dumplings of that time were mainly used as offerings to ancestors and spirits.
People wrapped rice dumplings into the shape of cow horns, ..
.. because the people at that time liked to use animals that had horns as offerings when they sacrificed.
They believed that animal horns were a spiritual thing to communicate between people and spirits.
Therefore, rice dumplings also had to be cow horn-shaped.
By the Sui and Tang dynasties, rice dumplings appeared in different shapes. They were rhombus, conical and so on.
At the Dragon Boat Festival people like to eat “Nine Rice Dumplings”,
This is nine rice dumplings tied together with brightly colored string, implying “many descendants”.
In the Song dynasty period, the inside filling of rice dumplings started getting plentiful.
They had ginkgo, red bean and so on inside.
In the later Ming and Qing dynasty periods, rice dumplings were assigned with auspicious connotations.
People liked to eat rice dumplings before exams at the imperial examinations, asking for a good omen.
For example, people that were participating in the exams at the imperial examinations, ..
.. would eat a rice dumpling with a red date filling before the exams.
That kind of rice dumplings is called “zao zong”, which is a homophone to “hit the mark soon”.
It implies “passing the provincial-level imperial examination soon”;
There were also people that liked to eat rice dumplings that were made into a pen shape.
“Bi zong” – “certainly hit the mark”, implies “to be bound to pass brilliantly”.
Rice dumplings have developed to this day, and very big changes have happened with both shape and flavor.
Present rice dumplings are long-shaped, square-shaped, rhombus, conical... there are all kinds of shapes.
Northern people eat sweet rice dumplings, southern people eat salty rice dumplings.
There are even bitter rice dumplings, spicy rice dumplings, sour rice dumplings, all kinds of flavors as well.
They really are very small rice dumplings that bear the weight of several thousand years of Chinese history and change!
